new_statements.quote: Vowels are weakened in a non-accented word-final position and may be deleted. Syllable structure is (C,)(C,)V. The possibilities at C, C, are pr, kr, mr, hr. Primary stress is assigned to the penultimate syllable of a word, and secondary stress to every alternate syllable before that.

new_statements.relation_note: Cluster-level phonology (after Migliazza 1972; table 13.2 headed 'In all four groups'): seven vowels, word-final unaccented vowels weakened, (C)(C)V syllables, primary stress on the penult with alternating secondary stress leftward.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress on the penultimate syllable of the word; secondary stress on every second syllable counting leftward from the penult (stated for the Yanomami dialect cluster as a whole).
new_statements.secondary_stress: alternating, every other syllable to the left of the penult
new_statements.exceptions: none in this passage (word-final unaccented vowels may weaken/delete)
new_statements.identity_note: group-level statement for the whole Yanomami dialect cluster; Yãnoma (Baixo Catrimani) was not recognized as a separate language in 1999 -- the Catrimani basin is assigned to the Yanomam 'southern subdialect' (p. 343); examples in the section are said to be from Yanomamɨ unless indicated [name in source: Yanomami dialect cluster (1a Yanomamɨ, 1b Yanomam incl. 'a southern [subdialect] in the Catrimani and Demeni river basins', 1c Yanam, 1d Sanuma); pages p. 343 (list), pp. 345-346 (§1.1.1 Phonology)]

sources.note: No phonology content. A language-policy booklet (schools, health, translation of signage/medicine leaflets, intergenerational transmission) written by Yanomami researchers; Yãnoma appears only in the enumeration of languages ('16. Yãnoma: Baixo Catrimani') and in a Yanomamɨ passage about the small Baixo-Catrimani group whose speech differs; a comparative line gives 'xama a' (tapir) per language but no Yãnoma form is legible. Nothing on accent, tone, syllables or sounds (decoded text searched for acento/tônic/sílaba/fonolog/pronúnc).

sources.citation: Ferreira, Helder Perri; Machado, Ana Maria Antunes; Senra, Estevão Benfica (orgs.). 2019. As línguas Yanomami no Brasil: diversidade e vitalidade. São Paulo/Boa Vista: Instituto Socioambiental / Hutukara Associação Yanomami (IPHAN). 216 pp. §1.4.5 Língua Yãnoma p. 55; §1.6 Comentários finais p. 71; ch. 3 comparative phonology pp. 60-63.
sources.note: Nothing on Yãnoma stress. States explicitly that Yãnoma 'não foi ainda documentada e descrita' (p. 55) and 'ainda carece totalmente de documentação e descrição' (p. 71); its language status rests only on mutual-intelligibility reports and oral history. Only Yãnoma data in the book are items in comparative wordlists (p. 123 ff.). The comparative phonology chapter mentions a Proto-Yanomami post-tonic syllable only in connection with Ninam codas (p. 62).

sources.citation: Rodrigues, Aryon Dall'Igna. 1986. Línguas brasileiras: para o conhecimento das línguas indígenas. São Paulo: Edições Loyola. 134 pp.
sources.note: Describes 'Yanomám ou Yainomá no leste e sueste da área, com dialetos no médio Catrimani, no alto Ajarani e no alto Apiaú'; comparative wordlist of Yanám/Sanumá/Yanomám/Yanomámi and sound correspondences (pp. 90-91); nothing on stress. The book's only prosodic statements concern Nambikwára, Múra and Pirahã tone (pp. 76-79).

sources.note: Gives comparative phoneme inventories for Ninam, Sanuma, Yanomam and Yainoma (p. 163: Yainoma consonants p t k th y[dz,ñ] s š h m n r w, vowels i u e a o ə with allophones), notes a non-phonemic glottal stop at word junctures, phonemic nasalization at word level, syllable types V, CV, CVC (+ restricted CCV, CCVC, VC), and then states only: 'As divergências fonológicas mais destacadas entre as quatro línguas são o acento vocabular, acento frasal e intonação' (p. 164) — i.e. word accent is said to differ across the four languages, but no placement rule or description of the accent is given for…

sources.citation: Salathé, Georges. 1932. Les Indiens Karimé. Revista del Instituto de Etnología de la Universidad Nacional de Tucumán 2: 297-316. (Glottolog refs 126928 / 56979; listed by Glottolog as an ethnographic work;wordlist; Glottolog language code 'Karimé = Yaroame [yro]'.)
sources.note: No phonology prose. The transcription key for the Karimé vocabulary (p. 314) defines diacritics, including an accent mark ("', marque l'accent"), length and 'open/closed pronunciation' signs; the c. 150-item Karimé word list (pp. 314-316) carries acute accents on many items (e.g. motúka 'soleil', kanôbori 'rame', yarnanãcci 'dormir'), i.e. accent MARKS in a wordlist without any statement of where accent falls — wordlist-only data, not a statement.
